condition: Find affordable products with useful features and positive customer feedback.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: The signal is product.price from product. The condition requires affordable products, so price is the direct attribute for affordability assessment. Starting from product, price is available on the stated path.

review.summary is a review-level text attribute on the review table. It can provide a concise expression of a customer's sentiment and mention of features, which is weakly indicative of positive customer feedback and possibly useful features, but it is not a product attribute and does not capture affordability. The signal is indirect for the product-level condition and does not connect to product.price, product.category, or product features.

The signal is customer.customer_name reachable from customer only. It provides no product attributes, price, features, rating, review text, or feedback. It cannot indicate affordability, usefulness, or positive customer feedback for products.

The signal is product.brand from product. The condition requires affordability, useful features, and positive customer feedback. Brand alone provides no evidence about price, features, or review sentiment, and the path is only product with no link to review or customer. No useful evidence for the condition.

The signal is product.category from product. The condition requires affordability, useful features, and positive customer feedback. Category alone provides no evidence about price affordability, feature usefulness, or review sentiment, and the path is only product with no link to review or customer.

The signal is product.description from product alone. It provides no price affordability, no feature usefulness, and no customer feedback. No relationship to review or customer is traversed, so it cannot support the condition.

The signal is product.title from product alone. Title provides no evidence about affordability, features, or customer feedback. No price, description, category, rating, review_text, or verified information is included, and no path to review or customer is used.

The signal is review.rating from review alone. It provides a positive feedback proxy but gives no product identity, no affordability, and no feature information. Without joining to product to get price/category/description/title and without any feature-related attribute, it cannot support the condition of affordable products with useful features and positive feedback.

The signal is review.review_text from review alone. It provides no product affordability, feature, or feedback linkage; no path to product or customer, and no rating or verification. It cannot support the condition.

The signal is review.review_time from review alone. Review time does not indicate affordability, product features, or positive customer feedback. No relationship to product price, features, or rating/summary is captured, so it provides no evidence for the condition.

The signal is review.verified from the review table alone. It provides no information about product affordability, features, or customer feedback sentiment, and the path does not reach product or customer attributes. Therefore it cannot support the condition.

condition: Show detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: review.review_text is the review's own text attribute on the review table. It directly contains the detailed narrative of a customer's real-world product experience, satisfying the condition.

The signal is customer.customer_name reachable from customer only. The user condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences, which needs review content attributes like review_text, summary, rating, review_time, verified and product context. customer_name alone provides no review text or product experience evidence and is not linked to review or product via the stated path.

The signal is product.brand from product. The user condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences, which is about review content such as review_text, summary, rating, review_time, verified. Product.brand is a product attribute with no path to review content, so it provides no evidence about the detail or real-world nature of reviews.

The signal is product.category from product. The user condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences, which is about review content such as review_text, summary, rating, review_time, verified. Product.category is a product-level attribute with no path to review content, so it provides no evidence about the detail or real-world nature of reviews.

The signal is product.description from product. The user condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences. The signal provides product description, not review content, and is not linked to review rows via the defined path. No evidence of review text, rating, review_time, summary, verified, or customer association is present.

The signal is product.price from product. The user condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences. Price is an attribute of product and provides no information about review content, review_text, summary, rating, verified, or review_time. No path connects price to review attributes, so the signal cannot support the condition.

The signal is product.title from product. The user condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences. The signal provides only a product title, with no path to review attributes such as review_text, rating, review_time, summary, verified, and no connection to customer. It does not capture review content or real-world experience evidence, so it offers no useful evidence for the condition.

The signal is review.rating from review. Rating is a numeric score and does not describe real-world product experiences. The condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world experiences, which would be captured by review_text, summary, or review_time, not by rating alone.
review.review_time is a timestamp attribute on review with no path to product or customer attributes. It provides no evidence about whether a review describes real-world product experiences.

The signal is review.summary from review. The condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences. Summary is a short attribute and does not guarantee detail or real-world experience description. No path to product or customer attributes is used, so no evidence of real-world experience is provided.

The signal is review.verified, which only indicates whether a review is verified. It does not provide any review content or description of real-world product experiences. The condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences, which would need review_text, summary, or similar content attributes, not just a boolean verified flag. Therefore the signal provides no useful evidence for the condition.

condition: Find reliable products from reputable brands with strong customer ratings.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: The signal is product.brand from product. The condition requires reputable brands and reliable products. Brand is a direct attribute of product and is the explicit brand signal needed to assess brand reputation; it is the starting entity for product reliability evaluation.

The signal is review.rating from review. The user condition requires strong customer ratings, and rating is the direct measure of customer rating strength. Path review is the starting entity, so the signal provides central, direct evidence for the rating component of the condition.

The signal is customer.customer_name reachable from customer only. It provides no product, brand, rating, or reliability information and does not connect to review or product tables, so it cannot support finding reliable products from reputable brands with strong customer ratings.

The signal is product.category from product. The user condition requires reliability, reputable brands, and strong customer ratings. Category alone provides no evidence about brand reputation, product reliability, or customer ratings, and the path starts only at product with no connection to review or customer. No useful evidence for the condition.

The signal is product.description from product. The condition requires reliability, reputable brands, and strong customer ratings. Description is a free-text product field with no direct link to brand reputation or rating evidence, and it does not connect to review.rating or review.verified or brand reputation signals. Therefore it provides no useful evidence for the stated condition.

The signal is product.price from product. Price is not a proxy for reliability, brand reputation, or customer ratings. The condition requires evidence about brand reputation and strong customer ratings; price provides no direct or indirect evidence for those criteria.

The signal is product.title from product alone. Title provides no information about brand reputation, rating strength, or reliability. No path to review or customer data is included, so the condition cannot be evaluated.

The signal is review.review_text from review alone. It provides no brand, product, or rating information and cannot identify reputable brands or strong customer ratings. No path to product or customer is included, so it cannot support the condition.

The signal is review.review_time from review alone. Review time provides no information about brand reputation, product reliability, or customer rating strength. It does not connect to product.brand, product attributes, or review.rating, so it cannot support the condition.

The signal is review.summary from review alone. It provides only a textual summary of a single review with no brand, product, rating, or reliability information, and no path to product or customer. It cannot support finding reliable products from reputable brands with strong customer ratings.

The signal is review.verified from the review table alone. It provides no brand, product, or rating information and does not connect to product or customer. It cannot support finding reliable products from reputable brands with strong customer ratings.

condition: Find negative reviews highlighting defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: The signal is customer.customer_name reachable from customer only. The condition requires negative reviews with defect/quality/performance mentions, which depend on review attributes (rating, review_text, summary, verified) and product context. Customer name provides no evidence about review sentiment or defect content, and the path does not reach review or product.

The signal is product.brand from product. The condition requires identifying negative reviews about defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance. Brand alone provides no information about review sentiment, review text content, or product quality issues, and the path starts at product without connecting to review attributes like rating, review_text, summary, or verified. No evidence linking brand to negative review characteristics is present in the schema.

The signal is product.category from product. The condition requires identifying negative reviews about defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance. Category alone provides no information about review sentiment, review text content, or product quality issues, and the signal path starts from product without connecting to review attributes like rating, review_text, summary, or verified. No evidence linking category to negative review content is present in the schema.

The signal is product.description from product. The user condition requires negative reviews highlighting defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance. The signal provides only product description text, with no path to review.rating, review.review_text, review.summary, or review.verified, and no connection to review content. Therefore it cannot provide evidence about negative reviews or their content.

The signal is product.price from product. The user condition requires identifying negative reviews about defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance. Price is not a review attribute and does not indicate sentiment or defect mentions. No path connects price to review_text, rating, or verified, so the signal provides no evidence for the condition.

The signal is product.title from product. The condition requires identifying negative reviews about defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance. Product title alone provides no information about review sentiment or defect content, and the signal path starts at product with no connection to review attributes like rating, review_text, summary, or verified. No evidence of negativity or defects is reachable from product.title.

The signal is only review.rating from the review table. Rating alone does not indicate whether a review highlights defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance, and the schema provides no mapping from rating values to those specific themes. No review_text, summary, or other content attributes are included, so the signal cannot capture the required negative defect/quality/performance focus.

The signal is only review.review_text from the review table with no path to product or customer. It provides no evidence about defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance, and no way to identify negative reviews.

review.review_time is a timestamp attribute on review with no relationship to sentiment, defects, quality, or performance. The condition requires identifying negative reviews about defects/poor quality/disappointing performance, which depends on review content (review_text, summary, rating, verified) and product/customer context, not on when the review was written. The signal provides no evidence toward the condition.

The signal is review.summary from review alone. The condition requires identifying negative reviews about defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance. Summary alone provides no sentiment or defect indication and no link to rating or review_text, so it cannot evidence the condition.

The signal is review.verified, which only indicates whether a review is verified. It does not capture review content or sentiment, so it provides no evidence about negative reviews highlighting defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance.

condition: Identify customers who write thoughtful, balanced, and informative reviews.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: The signal is review.review_text from the review table. Review text can contain content indicative of thoughtfulness, balance, and informativeness, but the signal is only the raw text with no derived features, length, or sentiment cues, so it provides useful but incomplete evidence for identifying customers who write thoughtful, balanced, informative reviews.
Signal is only customer.customer_name with path customer. No review attributes or review text are included, so it provides no evidence about thoughtfulness, balance, or informativeness of reviews.

The signal is product.brand reachable from product via review.product_id. Brand is a product attribute and provides no information about whether a review is thoughtful, balanced, and informative, nor about the customer who wrote it. No path connects brand to review content or customer writing style.

The signal is product.category from product, reached via review.product_id. Category is a product attribute and provides no information about whether a review is thoughtful, balanced, and informative, nor about the customer who wrote it. No review content or customer attributes are involved, so the signal carries no evidence for the condition.

The signal is product.description from product, reached via product. The user condition is about customers who write thoughtful, balanced, and informative reviews. Product description provides information about the product, not about the customer or the review content/quality. No path connects product.description to review attributes like review_text, rating, verified, or to customer. Therefore the signal gives no evidence for identifying customers with thoughtful, balanced, informative reviews.

The signal is product.price reachable from product via path product. The user condition requires identifying customers who write thoughtful, balanced, and informative reviews. Product price provides no evidence about review thoughtfulness, balance, or informativeness, nor about the customer author. No relationship to review content or customer writing style is captured.

The signal is product.title from product, reached via product path. The user condition requires identifying customers who write thoughtful, balanced, informative reviews. Product title provides no information about review quality or customer writing style, and the signal does not involve review attributes or customer identity. No plausible evidence for the condition.

The signal is review.rating from review alone. Rating is a numeric score and does not capture thoughtfulness, balance, or informativeness of review text. No path to review_text, summary, or verified, and no customer linkage is used, so it provides no evidence for the condition.
review.review_time is a timestamp attribute on review with no path to customer or product content. It provides no evidence about thoughtfulness, balance, or informativeness of review text.

The signal is review.summary from review. The condition requires identifying customers who write thoughtful, balanced, and informative reviews. The summary attribute alone provides no evidence of thoughtfulness, balance, or informativeness, and the signal is not linked to customer via review.customer_id. No useful schema evidence is present.

review.verified is a boolean flag about purchase verification; it does not capture thoughtfulness, balance, or informativeness of review content. No path to review_text, summary, rating, or customer attributes is used, so the signal provides no evidence for the condition.

condition: Find products that are similar in their purpose, features, and the needs they address, even when their descriptions use different terminology.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Brand is a product attribute reachable via product. Brand can indicate product family or manufacturer style, providing a weak proxy for purpose/features, but brand alone does not capture purpose, features, or needs and is confounded by diverse product lines under one brand. Limited direct evidence for similarity in purpose/features/needs.

product.category is a direct attribute of the starting product table. Category can group items by broad purpose or type, providing a weak proxy for similarity in purpose/features/needs, but it is coarse and does not capture nuanced feature or need overlap or terminology differences.

The signal is product.description from the product table. Description text can provide purpose, features, and needs terminology, but similarity based on different wording requires semantic matching beyond raw description alone. It offers weak, indirect evidence for finding similar products.

The signal is product.title from the product table with no joins. Title can provide a weak semantic cue about purpose/features, but alone it is a single short text field and does not capture description, category, brand, or review-derived usage signals needed to judge similarity across different terminology.

review.summary is a review-level text attribute on review. It can provide weak semantic cues about a product’s purpose/features via the review’s wording, but it is indirect, noisy, and not a product attribute; similarity must be inferred from many reviews and is confounded by reviewer language. Path is review only, with no link to product attributes beyond review.product_id, so evidence for product similarity is weak.

The signal is customer.customer_name reachable from customer only. The user condition requires product similarity by purpose/features/needs, which needs product attributes and review content. Customer name provides no product or review information and no path to product or review, so it cannot support the condition.

The signal is product.price from product. Price is a numeric cost attribute and does not capture purpose, features, or needs addressed, nor does it provide semantic similarity of descriptions. No path to review text or product description features is used, so it cannot indicate similarity in purpose/features/needs despite different terminology.

The signal is review.rating from review alone. Rating provides no product purpose, features, or needs information and does not connect to product attributes or description terminology. No evidence for similarity in purpose/features/needs.

The signal is review.review_text from the review table alone. It provides only the review text attribute with no path to product or customer, so it cannot link reviews to products or establish similarity between products. No product attributes or relationships are included, so the signal gives no evidence for finding products similar in purpose, features, or needs.

review.review_time is a timestamp on a review row. It provides no information about product purpose, features, or needs, nor about similarity between products. The path starts and ends at review with no link to product attributes or description terminology, so it cannot support the condition.

The signal is review.verified from the review table alone. Verified indicates whether a review is from a verified purchase, which provides no information about product purpose, features, or needs, nor about similarity between products. No path connects to product attributes or description terminology, so the signal cannot support finding similar products.

condition: Find products that appeal to similar groups of customers based on their purchasing and reviewing behavior, even if the products belong to different categories.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Signal is customer.customer_name from customer table alone. No product linkage, no review linkage, no purchasing or reviewing behavior. Cannot identify products or customer groups, so provides no evidence for products appealing to similar customer groups across categories.

The signal is product.brand from product alone. It provides no information about customers, purchasing or reviewing behavior, and cannot link products to similar customer groups or across categories. No relationship to review or customer is used.

The signal is product.category from product alone. The condition requires identifying products that appeal to similar customer groups based on purchasing and reviewing behavior across categories. Category provides no information about customers, reviews, or cross-category customer overlap, so it cannot support the requested similarity.

The signal is product.description from product alone. It provides no information about customers, purchasing or reviewing behavior, and cannot link products via shared customer groups. No relationship to review or customer is used, so it cannot support finding products that appeal to similar customer groups.

The signal is product.price from product alone. Price is a product attribute with no path to review or customer, so it provides no evidence about customer groups, purchasing or reviewing behavior, or cross-category appeal based on shared customers. The condition requires customer-based similarity; price alone cannot indicate similar customer groups.

The signal is product.title from product alone. It provides only the product name with no customer, review, or purchase behavior linkage, so it cannot indicate which customer groups appeal to the product or enable similarity across categories.

The signal is review.rating from review alone. It provides no product or customer linkage and no way to compare groups of customers across products, so it cannot support finding products that appeal to similar customer groups.

The signal is review.review_text from review alone. It provides only the text of a single review with no product, customer, or linking information in the path, so it cannot identify products, customers, or groups, nor relate products across categories.

review.review_time is a timestamp on a review row. It provides no information about which customers bought or reviewed which products, nor about customer groups or cross-category similarity. The signal is isolated to review and does not connect to product or customer attributes needed to infer similar customer groups.

The signal is review.summary from review alone. It provides only a textual summary of a single review with no link to product identity, customer identity, or any cross-product aggregation. Without product_id, customer_id, or any relationship traversal, it cannot identify products, group customers, or compare purchasing/reviewing behavior across products or categories. Therefore it offers no evidence for finding products that appeal to similar customer groups.

The signal is review.verified from the review table alone. It provides no product or customer linkage and no information about groups of customers, purchasing or reviewing behavior, or cross-category similarity. No path connects to product or customer, so it cannot support the condition.

condition: Find customer reviews that provide detailed, credible, and useful insights into a product's strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: review.review_text is the primary content carrier for detailed, credible, and useful insights about a product's strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance. Starting from review, the text field directly provides the narrative evidence needed to assess usefulness, though credibility and detail level still require interpretation beyond the raw text alone.

review.summary is a short headline from the review table. It can hint at sentiment or a key point but is too brief to convey detailed, credible, useful insights about strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance; the full review_text is needed for depth.

The signal is customer.customer_name from the customer table with no path to review or product. Customer name alone provides no evidence about review detail, credibility, usefulness, or product strengths/weaknesses/performance. No relationship to review attributes such as rating, review_text, review_time, summary, verified, nor to product attributes.

The signal is product.brand from product. Brand alone does not indicate whether a review is detailed, credible, or useful, nor does it describe strengths, weaknesses, or real-world performance. No review attributes or review content are involved, so the signal provides no evidence for the condition.

The signal is product.category from product. Category alone does not indicate whether a review is detailed, credible, useful, or discusses strengths, weaknesses, or real-world performance. No review attributes or review-product linkage is used.

The signal is product.description from product. The user condition requires detailed, credible, useful customer reviews about strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance. Product description is a product attribute, not a review attribute, and provides no evidence about review detail, credibility, or usefulness, nor about real-world performance from customers.

The signal is product.price from product. Price is a product attribute and does not describe review content, credibility, detail, or real-world performance insights. No path connects price to review attributes like review_text, rating, verified, or review_time, so it provides no evidence for detailed, credible, useful customer reviews about strengths, weaknesses, and performance.

The signal is product.title from product. The user condition requires detailed, credible, useful insights about strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance from customer reviews. Product title alone provides no review content, credibility, or performance insight, and does not connect to review attributes like rating, review_text, verified, or review_time. No evidence for the condition.

The signal is only review.rating from the review table. Rating alone does not indicate detail, credibility, usefulness, or coverage of strengths, weaknesses, and real-world performance. No review_text, summary, verified, review_time, or product/customer context is included, so the signal provides no evidence for the condition.

review.review_time is a timestamp attribute on review with no path to product strengths, weaknesses, or performance content. It provides no evidence about detail, credibility, or usefulness of insights.

The signal is review.verified alone. Verified indicates purchase verification but provides no information about detail, credibility of content, or usefulness regarding strengths, weaknesses, or real-world performance. No review_text, rating, summary, review_time, or product/customer attributes are included, so the signal cannot support the condition.

condition: Find products that offer particularly good value for money by balancing affordability, perceived quality, and customer satisfaction.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: review.summary is a free-text field on review. It can provide qualitative cues about perceived quality and satisfaction, but it is not a structured measure of affordability, price, or quality, and it is not aggregated. Alone it gives only weak, indirect evidence for value-for-money balancing.

customer.customer_name is a name string with no link to affordability, quality, or satisfaction. The path starts at customer and provides only the name, which does not capture price, perceived quality, or customer satisfaction for products.

The signal is product.brand from product. Brand alone provides no information about affordability, perceived quality, or customer satisfaction. No price, rating, review_text, or other quality/satisfaction attributes are included, and no path to review or customer is used. Therefore it cannot support the value-for-money condition.

The signal is product.category alone. Category provides only a grouping label with no information about affordability, perceived quality, or customer satisfaction. It does not connect to price, rating, review_text, verified, or any customer data, so it cannot support the value-for-money condition.

The signal is product.description from product. Description is a free-text marketing field with no numeric or structured quality, price, or satisfaction information. It provides no evidence for affordability, perceived quality, or customer satisfaction, and cannot support value-for-money assessment.

The signal is product.price alone. The condition requires balancing affordability, perceived quality, and customer satisfaction. Price alone provides no information about perceived quality or customer satisfaction, and cannot by itself indicate value for money. No evidence of quality or satisfaction is reachable from this signal.

The signal is product.title from product alone. Title provides no information about affordability, perceived quality, or customer satisfaction. No price, rating, review_text, or other value-related attributes are included, and the path contains only product with no joins to review or customer. Therefore it cannot support the value-for-money condition.

The signal is review.rating from review alone. It provides perceived quality/customer satisfaction but gives no product affordability information and no product identity linkage in the signal definition. Without product price or a path to product, it cannot support balancing affordability with perceived quality and satisfaction for products.

The signal is review.review_text from review alone. It provides only free-form text with no affordability, quality, or satisfaction metrics, and no link to product price, brand, category, or customer. No path connects to product attributes or aggregated satisfaction, so it cannot support value-for-money balancing.

review.review_time is a timestamp on the review table with no path to product price, brand, category, description, title, or to review rating, review_text, summary, verified. The condition requires affordability, perceived quality, and customer satisfaction, which need product price and review rating/text signals. Review time alone provides no evidence for value for money.

The signal is review.verified from the review table alone. It provides no product affordability, quality, or customer satisfaction information and does not connect to product attributes or aggregate customer sentiment. It cannot support identifying products with good value for money.

condition: Find customers who have similar preferences and expectations, as reflected in the products they review, the opinions they express, and the aspects of products they care about.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: The signal is only customer.customer_name from the customer table with no path to review or product. It provides no information about reviewed products, opinions, or cared aspects, so it cannot support finding customers with similar preferences and expectations.

The signal is product.brand reachable from product only. The user condition requires customers with similar preferences and expectations reflected in products they review, opinions they express, and aspects they care about. Starting from product and using brand provides no customer linkage and no review content or opinion aspects, so it cannot evidence customer similarity.

The signal is product.category reachable from product only. The user condition requires customers with similar preferences and expectations as reflected in products they review, opinions they express, and aspects they care about. Starting from a product and using its category provides no connection to customers, review opinions, or aspects, so it cannot support the condition.

Signal is product.description from product table. Starting entity is customer. Path is product only, with no link from customer to product. No review join is specified, so the signal cannot be reached from customer and provides no evidence about customers preferences, opinions, or aspects they care about.

The signal is product.price reachable from product via path product. The user condition requires customers with similar preferences and expectations as reflected in products they review, opinions they express, and aspects they care about. Price alone from product provides no customer linkage and no opinion or aspect information, so it cannot support identifying similar customers.

Signal is product.title from product table with no path to customer. The condition requires customers linked via reviews and their expressed opinions/aspects. Product title alone provides no customer linkage and no review content, so it cannot support finding customers with similar preferences.

The signal is review.rating from review alone. It provides only a single review's rating with no customer identity, no product context, and no textual opinions or aspects. It cannot link reviews to customers or products, so it cannot support finding customers with similar preferences, expectations, opinions, or cared-about aspects.

The signal is review.review_text from review alone. It provides the opinion text for a single review but does not connect reviews to customers or products, nor does it capture product attributes or aspects. No path links to customer or product, so it cannot identify customers with similar preferences or expectations.

review.review_time is a timestamp on a review row. It provides no information about product preferences, expressed opinions, or cared aspects, and does not connect reviews to other customers or products beyond the review itself. No evidence for similarity of preferences or expectations.

The signal is review.summary from review alone. It provides a single review's summary text but no link to the customer or product, and no way to compare across reviews or customers. The condition requires identifying customers with similar preferences across products, opinions, and cared aspects, which needs customer identity and product context. The signal lacks customer_id, product_id, and any cross-review aggregation, so it cannot support similarity between customers.

The signal is review.verified alone, with no path to customer or product. It provides no information about which customers reviewed which products, the opinions expressed, or product aspects they care about, so it cannot support finding customers with similar preferences and expectations.

condition: I'm looking for products that serve similar purposes, regardless of their brand or category.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: The signal is customer.customer_name reachable from customer only. It provides no product attributes, no review content, and no linkage to product purpose, brand, or category. Therefore it cannot indicate products that serve similar purposes.

The signal is product.brand from product. Brand is explicitly excluded by the user condition 'regardless of their brand or category', so brand provides no useful evidence for finding products that serve similar purposes.

The signal is product.category from product. The user condition asks for products that serve similar purposes regardless of brand or category. Category is explicitly to be ignored, so category provides no useful evidence for similar purpose and is contrary to the condition.

The signal is product.description from product alone. No similarity or purpose information is captured, and no relationship to other products is provided. Cannot support finding products with similar purposes.

The signal is product.price from product. Price is not a purpose or functional similarity indicator and the schema provides no attributes or relationships that describe product purpose, use case, or functional equivalence. No path from product to purpose-related information exists, so price cannot provide evidence for products serving similar purposes.

The signal is product.title from product alone. Title is a product attribute but provides no relationship to other products or purpose similarity; no path connects products to each other or to purpose information. Cannot support finding similar-purpose products regardless of brand or category.

The signal is review.rating from review alone. Rating provides no information about product purpose, similarity, brand, or category, and the path does not reach product attributes. No evidence for products serving similar purposes.

The signal is review.review_text from the review table alone. It provides no product linkage, no similarity features, and no brand/category information to compare products. No path to product is included, so it cannot support finding products with similar purposes.

review.review_time is a timestamp on a review row. It provides no information about product purpose, similarity, or functional attributes, and the path starts and ends at review with no link to product features. Therefore it cannot support finding products that serve similar purposes.

The signal is review.summary from the review table only. It provides no product linkage, no purpose or functional description, and no way to compare products for similarity of purpose. No attributes from product are included, so the signal cannot support finding products with similar purposes regardless of brand or category.

The signal is review.verified from the review table alone. It provides no product attributes, no similarity features, and no linkage to purpose or functional equivalence. With only verified flag and no path to product features or related reviews, it cannot indicate products that serve similar purposes regardless of brand or category.

condition: Which products appeal to similar customers based on their reviewing behavior?

signals.evidence: The signal is customer.customer_name from the customer table with no path to review or product. It provides only a name for a starting customer and no reviewing behavior or product linkage, so it cannot support finding products that appeal to similar customers.

condition: Show me reviews that provide useful insights into a product's strengths and weaknesses.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: review.review_text is the review's own text attribute on the review table. The condition asks for reviews that provide useful insights into a product's strengths and weaknesses, which is directly expressed in the review text. Starting from review and using review.review_text gives the central content needed to assess insights.

The signal is customer.customer_name reachable via customer table only. It provides no information about review content, product strengths or weaknesses, and does not connect to review or product attributes. No evidence for usefulness of reviews.

The signal is product.brand from product. Brand alone does not indicate whether a review provides useful insights into a product's strengths and weaknesses. No review attributes or review content are involved, so the signal gives no evidence about review usefulness.
